description:
FILED s471a (Opus, 2026-09-06), by a #1271 probe.  PRE-EXISTING, and on the
SUCCESS path -- so it is not #1271's failure-path autovivification.

    my @a; my $ok = open($a[0], "<", "/etc/hostname") ? 1 : 0;
    my $l = <$a[0]>;
    perl : ok=1 got=yes
    PCL  : ok=1 got=no        <-- the open reports success and the read gets undef

    my %h; my $ok = open($h{k}, "<", "/etc/hostname") ? 1 : 0;
    my $l = readline($h{k});
    perl : ok=1 got=yes
    PCL  : ok=1 got=yes       <-- the HASH element spelling works

So `open` reports success, `$!` is untouched, and the handle is simply not
where the program looks for it: a silent wrong of the worst kind, because the
`or die` a careful program writes does not fire.

The failure spelling diverges the same way and for the same reason (probes K07
/K08, s471a): `open($a[0], "<", $missing)` leaves `defined($a[0])` 0 where perl
says 1.  Fixing the underlying place-passing fixes both.

START AT `%p-fh-arg` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): it decides what `open`'s first
argument becomes.  The question to answer FIRST is whether an array-element
place arrives as a BOX (which %p-install-fh could box-set) or as a VALUE -- the
hash-element case working says the two element accessors disagree, which is the
rule-11 smell.  Probe `readline($a[0])` as well as `<$a[0]>`: the hash case was
only measured through `readline`, so the angle-bracket READ path may be the
divergent half rather than the store.

=== DONE (s473f) ===
FIXED, and THE TASK'S PREMISE WAS WRONG in an instructive way.  The STORE was
never the problem and the hash spelling did not "work": BOTH element spellings
landed the stream under the shared `*p-undef*` KEYWORD in *p-filehandles*
(`p-aref`/`p-gethash` hand back that keyword for an empty slot, and
%p-install-fh's last arm takes anything that is not a box for a handle NAME).
`readline($h{k})` "worked" only because it looked the SAME wrong key up again
-- and an unrelated `readline($b[0])` on a never-opened element read the FIRST
file's lines (scratch/s473f/p1d-undefcorrupt.pl).

`<$a[0]>` is NOT a readline at all: perlop says a `<...>` that is not a simple
scalar is a GLOB, and perl answers the stringified handle ("GLOB(0x...)").
PCL's `p-glob` lowering was right all along; the probe that read `defined $l`
could not see the difference.

FIX: %p-fh-arg gains a fourth slot kind, :INSTALL -- everything :T means, plus
an element read accessor rewritten to its eager `-box` twin through the one map
+p-elem-place-box-accessor+ (the same four heads p-setf's refaliasing arm
enumerates).  The seven openers (open, sysopen, opendir, pipe, socket,
socketpair, accept's new handle) go through one wrapper %p-fh-install-arg,
which also refuses an UNDEF designator with perl's own death.
%p-resolve-dh unifies the dirhandle resolver (readdir/closedir/rewinddir each
carried a two-armed copy while %p-dirhandle-path carried a three-armed one, so
an element dirhandle opened fine and then read NOTHING).

Guard Pl/t/handle-place-01.t (155 rows, perl as oracle).  ir-conform 308-io and
309-io left known-fail.  Commit a3d13bce.
subject: open($a[0], ...) SUCCEEDS but <$a[0]> reads nothing: an ARRAY-ELEMENT place never receives the handle (the hash-element spelling works)
